claims.text: The initial alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state.
A 5 μm Al2O3 surface coating will improve the oxygen resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr at high temperature.
The coating will preserve the alloy's useful mechanical performance.
The Al2O3 coating acts as a diffusion barrier.
The Al2O3 coating reduces oxygen diffusion into HfNbTaTiZr.
Reduced oxygen diffusion minimizes oxidation of the alloy.
Reduced oxygen diffusion minimizes oxidation-related degradation of mechanical properties.
After exposure in air for 500 hours at temperatures up to 1000 °C, the coated alloy will show 30% less oxidation-induced mass gain than uncoated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coated alloy's yield strength will remain within 10% of the uncoated baseline under strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The baseline yield-strength range is 163–530 MPa.
Previous studies have established the effectiveness of Al2O3 coatings as oxygen-diffusion barriers.
The predicted oxidation and strength changes are based on estimates from similar coating systems.

contradictions.description: The conditions define a maximum temperature of 1000 °C, whereas the boundary separately defines a maximum of 1100 °C.

A 30% reduction predicts coated mass gain equal to 70% of the uncoated value, but the stated rule literally falsifies the hypothesis if coated mass gain is greater than 20% relative to the uncoated value. Thus, the predicted result itself would exceed the stated falsification threshold unless 'greater than 20%' was intended to mean a 20% increase rather than 20% of the control.
